issues.claim: Round 5 makes the why answer's `plan` section read the view's drawn week (R5-08 (d): base §11.2's `why` member, V10 §2.13 `rows(…, opts: { view?: WhyView })`, V03 §4.6), and V09 §5.8 (l. 4025) now reads "its damage lines at the building's own level and the drawn week of the view the card opens on"; V07 §4.5's crisis, season and festival rows already read the view (R4-05). V09 §2.12's `WhyCardModel` row (l. 986) rebuilds the answer only "at every open and on `doc.changed` naming the subject", and V09 §2.7 (l. 620–622, 667) re-asks a cached answer only at `onEffectiveKey`. The card is non-modal (§5.8), so it stays open across a timeline scrub, a Season change, a festival or crisis preview; §2.12's damage-lines row (l. 1010) says the card's `plan` section is "recomputed at … each week change", which the `WhyCardModel` row contradicts, and nothing re-reads V07's view-bound rows at a `yearWeek`, `festival` or `crises` change. One builder re-asks `why` at each view change; another leaves the card stating the week it opened on while the map draws another. T-V9-86's scrubbed-week clause passes either way when the card is opened after the scrub.
issues.required_change: (1) V09 §2.7, after "… reads that view's week, year position, festival, crises and looks.": "While its card or panel is open, a view-bound answer is re-asked at each change of that view's §2.9 `week`, `yearWeek`, `festival` or `crises` — a scrub, the Season control, a festival or crisis preview, **Show crises** — as a cached answer is at `onEffectiveKey`, so V07 §4.5's crisis, season and festival rows and V03 §4.6's `plan` damage rows state the view on screen." (2) V09 §2.12's `WhyCardModel` row, regenerate cell: "rebuilt at every open and on `doc.changed` naming the subject" → "rebuilt at every open, on `doc.changed` naming the subject, at `onEffectiveKey` and at each change of its view's `week`, `yearWeek`, `festival` or `crises` (V09 §2.7)". (3) V09 §5.8: "at the building's own level and the drawn week of the view the card opens on" → "at the building's own level and its view's drawn week, re-read as the week changes (V09 §2.7)". (4) T-V9-86's last clause adds "; with the card left open while the timeline is scrubbed, its `plan` section follows each drawn week".

issues.claim: Round 5 gives the why line and the card's `ruinedFor` row five forms each (V09 §4.9 l. 2201; §4.21.12 (4) l. 3637–3644). Row 90 (l. 1610) lists "a condition the dossier names not" and "a condition with neither a name nor an `untilWeek`", outcomes `info.crisis.lineUnnamed` and `info.crisis.lineUnnamedOpen`, its test cell T-V9-85. T-V9-85 (l. 4436) runs the named line ("{look}: {condition}, weeks {a}–{b}"), the preview's card row ("For now: Ruined quarters — a preview") and "a look with no `untilWeek` the open form", but no unnamed form: `lineUnnamed` and `lineUnnamedOpen` are run by no V09 bar, and `ruinedForUnnamed` and `ruinedForUnnamedOpen` by no bar in the set (a census finds them only in V09 §4.9 and §4.21.12 (4); V10's T-V10-52 runs `.lineUnnamed` and `.lineUnnamedOpen` as the clerk's `says` key, not V09's card or its `ruinedFor` row). A card that words an unnamed look by the named form, its `{condition}` empty, passes every bar (R5-01's grading: an untested edge whose outcome the text defines).

issues.claim: Round 5 gives V09's why card a famine's bare field (R5-08 (c): §11.2's `looks` `field`, each famine entry's `over`; V09 §4.21.12 (4) l. 3652–3654; row 90), and §4.21.12 (4) closes "Volume 10's explanation renders the same keys" (l. 3656). V10 sends no field (§3.5 l. 1458: a `building` naming none "is not passed"; §3.23 row 34: "a field … `over` absent"), and V10 §3.9b (8) defines only *A house under a disaster look* (l. 2046). At the town rungs the card's famine row is the card's own, read from the `looks` reader, not a `WhyAnswer` row, so the clerk explaining a field under a famine has neither the row nor a read telling a bare field from a sown one: its outcome for "why is this field bare?" is undefined, and it may lay a sown, or seasonally bare (item 117), field to the famine. Off the common path, hence minor.
